comments.content: `updateActivityComponent` does not handle the `mode` prop for visibility. Unlike `updateOffscreenComponent`, it never sets `workInProgress.memoizedState` or `workInProgress.flags` based on `nextMode`. As a result, `<Activity mode="hidden">` will always render its children as visible, and the Offscreen fiber's `memoizedState` will be `null`, which can break downstream logic (e.g., `updateOffscreenComponent`/`completeWork`/`commitWork` paths that read `memoizedState`). Consider delegating to `updateOffscreenComponent` (or replicating its mode handling) so hidden mode actually hides children.

The `updateActivityComponent` branch does not handle `workInProgress.ref` cleanup or `workInProgress.flags` for refs. `updateOffscreenComponent` sets `workInProgress.flags |= Ref` when the ref changes; here the ref is copied onto the child fragment but the parent fiber's ref flag is never set, so refs on `<Activity>` may not be attached/detached correctly.

`updateActivityComponent` ignores `renderLanes` in the update path and does not bail out when props are unchanged. `updateOffscreenComponent` includes a `bailoutOffscreenComponent` fast path; without it, every render of an Activity will re-render its subtree even when nothing changed.

The `offscreenChildProps` object is recreated on every render and passed to `updateWorkInProgressOffscreenFiber`, which will mark the child as having new pending props each time. This defeats memoization/bailout for the child fragment. Consider reusing `currentChild.pendingProps`/`memoizedProps` when `nextMode` and `nextChildren` are unchanged.

`updateActivityComponent` does not handle the case where `current.child` is not an Offscreen fiber (e.g., after a previous render produced a different child type). `updateWorkInProgressOffscreenFiber` assumes the current child is an Offscreen fiber; if not, it will produce an invalid work-in-progress. Consider asserting or falling back to a fresh mount.

Adding `ActivityComponent` to the fallthrough case that includes `LazyComponent`, `FunctionComponent`, etc. means `completeWork` will call `bubbleProperties(workInProgress)` and return `null` without handling the Offscreen-specific completion logic (e.g., `updateOffscreenComponent`'s `memoizedState`/`flags` handling in `completeWork`). Since `ActivityComponent` wraps an Offscreen child, the Offscreen child will still complete, but the Activity fiber itself will not propagate any Offscreen-related flags. Verify this is intentional; if Activity is meant to behave like Offscreen, it likely needs its own completion handling.

`createFiberFromActivity` does not set `fiber.stateNode` (unlike `createFiberFromOffscreen`, which sets `fiber.stateNode = primaryChildInstance`). If any downstream code (e.g., commit phase, DevTools) expects `stateNode` on Offscreen-like fibers, this will be `null`. Confirm whether Activity fibers need a `stateNode`.

`REACT_ACTIVITY_TYPE` is routed to `renderOffscreen`, which reads `props.mode` and `props.children`. Since `Activity` uses the same `mode`/`children` shape this is fine, but note that `renderOffscreen` may also check `props.mode === 'hidden'` and set `task.blockedSegment`/postponement behavior. Ensure the Activity element's `mode` prop is validated the same way as Offscreen (e.g., only 'hidden'/'visible') to avoid silently treating invalid modes as visible.

Changing `unstable_Activity` from `REACT_OFFSCREEN_TYPE` to `REACT_ACTIVITY_TYPE` is a breaking change for any code that relied on the previous symbol identity (e.g., `element.type === React.unstable_Activity` comparisons against `REACT_OFFSCREEN_TYPE`, or serialized element types). This is likely intentional for the new Activity component, but it should be called out in the changelog/release notes.

`REACT_ACTIVITY_TYPE` is added unconditionally, while `REACT_OFFSCREEN_TYPE` is also unconditional. If Activity is meant to be gated behind a feature flag (like `enableLegacyHidden` for LegacyHidden), consider gating it similarly to avoid exposing an experimental type in stable builds.
